newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish largest Plock refinery raises fuel prices.
newsitem.headline: Polish largest Plock refinery raises fuel prices.

text.p: Poland's biggest Plock refinery on Friday raised its diesel and gasoline prices by 4.9 and 0.7 percent respectively in line with a new finance ministry regulation, Plock's chief financial officer said.
Marek Mroczkowski told Reuters the price rise should improve the supply of diesel fuel in Poland although it would not solve problems with gasoline.
"On October 11 the price of diesel from Plock rises by six grosz per litre for distributors, which will result in their rising of prices by 4.9 percent to 1.28 zlotys per litre," Mroczkowski said.
"However, decisions concerning petrol do not change anything because they allow for only a one grosz rise per litre and do not improve the profitability of domestic production or imports."

The ministry, which controls fuel prices, raised the maximum diesel price by 4.9 percent to 1.28 zlotys per litre, and by 0.7 percent to 1.51 zlotys and 1.66 zlotys respectively for 94 octane leaded and 95 octane unleaded gasoline.

The regulation came into force on Wednesday and runs until the end of the year. The ministry also cut the excise tax on imported and domestically produced diesel fuel by 60 zlotys per tonne to 400 zlotys and 360 zlotys respectively.
The rise of world oil prices in recent months has hit hard Polish importers and producers, who are bound by official caps on fuel prices.

The finance ministry was long reluctant to rise official ceilings, fearing such a move would be inflationary and upset the official 17 percent inflation target for this year. --Jan Strupczewski +48 22 653 9700
